did_you_know.text: Did you know? Nahash the Ammonite besieged Jabesh-gilead, and the men of the city asked to make a treaty with him to avoid war.
Did you know? The condition Nahash proposed was to gouge out the right eye of every man of Jabesh-gilead, and he described it as a disgrace upon all Israel.

Did you know? The elders of Jabesh-gilead asked Nahash for seven days so they could send messengers throughout the territory of Israel and seek a deliverer; only if no one could be found would they surrender to him.

Did you know? When Saul heard the report of the men of Jabesh, the Spirit of God came powerfully upon him, and he became very angry; this describes his transition from the fields to leading the people.

Did you know? Saul rallied Israel with a striking symbolic message: he cut up a pair of oxen and sent the pieces throughout the territory of Israel, and the people went out as one, filled with the fear of the LORD.
Did you know? The army counted at Bezek included three hundred thousand men from Israel and thirty thousand men from Judah.
Did you know? Saul divided the people into three companies, and they attacked the Ammonite camp during the morning watch, until the survivors scattered and no two of them remained together.
Did you know? After the victory, the people wanted to put Saul’s opponents to death, but Saul refused, saying that no one should be put to death on the day the LORD had brought deliverance to Israel.
Did you know? After the deliverance at Jabesh-gilead, the people renewed Saul’s kingship at Gilgal before the LORD, offered fellowship offerings, and rejoiced greatly.
